retrospective.harder_than_needed: The BACKLOG finding framed both halves (bunker-before-port ordering AND serve-worker leak) as open, but the serve half had already shipped in commits a334194/86dea56. The fixer spent verification effort confirming a no-op. Findings promoted from old reports should be re-validated against current HEAD before dispatch.

root_cause: In e2e/global-setup.ts, assertPortFree(3100) was called at step 3 (former line 301), AFTER bunkers A, B, and C were already spawned at steps 257-296. When port 3100 was held, setup threw on the port check, but three live bunker.mjs children had already started and were untracked: .state.json had not yet been written (it was written last, at the end), so globalTeardown had no PIDs to clean up. The three bunkers were re-parented to init and kept holding NIP-46 subscriptions on the test relay, starving subsequent runs (the same failure mode cleanupOrphans was built to mop up). The serve-worker-leak half of the report was ALREADY fixed before this task: serve is spawned directly from node_modules/.bin (not via npx), with detached:true, and teardown kills the process group (commits a334194 'kill serve via process group' and 86dea56). That half was verified as already-correct and left unchanged.
fix: Extracted the orderable region (generate keys -> port check -> spawn 3 bunkers -> spawn serve -> HTTP health check -> write .state.json) into an exported prepareServers(deps) function with injectable dependencies (spawnBunker, spawnServe, assertPortFree, waitForHttp, writeState, writeKeys). Moved assertPortFree(3100) to the FRONT of that sequence, before any bunker spawn, so a busy port aborts with zero spawned children. .state.json is still written only after all four processes are live, so a mid-setup abort leaves the file absent. globalSetup now calls prepareServers() with production defaults; its build/platform steps are unchanged.

notes: The serve-leak half of the original report was already resolved in git history; this task's net new fix is the bunker-before-port-check ordering. The dependency-injection seam (PrepareDeps) was the minimal change needed to make the ordering unit-testable without running next build, make ensure-platform, a relay, or real child processes.
caveats: ACCEPTED over a Codex `high` adjacent-hardening finding (adjudicated by Decider, opus). The finding flags (a) TOCTOU between assertPortFree and spawnServe and (b) no try/catch around the bunker B/C/serve spawn sequence. Both describe leaks bounded to ~1s and self-healing via bunker.mjs's PPID watchdog + cleanupOrphans sweep — categorically different from the original indefinite 3-bunker leak this contract fixes. Out of contract scope (single-host/single-run model per CLAUDE.md). Recommended as a separate low/medium 'e2e harness hardening' follow-up finding (synchronous spawn-sequence cleanup; port reservation only if the concurrent-run model ever changes).
